newsitem.title: USA: LDC debt dips with US Treasuries after dollar fall.
newsitem.headline: LDC debt dips with US Treasuries after dollar fall.

text.p: Most emerging market debt prices fell in sympathy with U.S. Treasuries on Friday after hedge-fund selling of dollar positions, traders said.
"We're mainly just lower here with Treasuries," one Brady bond trader said.
Treasuries rebounded late amid a flight to quality out of the U.S. stock market, trader said.
Losses spread fairly evenly across the emerging debt market. Profit-taking added to the losses of issues that rose strongly on Thursday, traders said.
Brazil "C" bonds lost 1-1/4 to stand at 83 after rising a full point on Thursday, while Mexico's UMS 2026 global bond fell 1-3/4 to 120-1/2 to erase much of its gains from the day before.
In other Latin America bonds, Argentina FRBs slipped 1/2 lower to 95-1/4, while Mexico Pars fell 7/8 to 80-1/4.

Argentine Economy Minister Roque Fernandez on Friday said his country may be unable to reach an agreement with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) on fiscal targets and structural reforms before late September.
Denis Perisien, a Latin America economist with Bankers Trust, said the announcement probably would not shake investors' confidence because economic fundamentals remain so strong in Argentina.
"The economy has certainly performed better than expected," Perisien said.
Elsewhere, dollar-denominated Russian Vnesh loans fell 1/2 to 101-5/8 and Bulgaria FLRBs eased 1/8 to 63-1/4.
"It's been a typical slow Friday in August," one trader said.
U.S. Treasuries dove in early trading amid concerns about the dollar, which dropped on expectations of higher German interest rates, traders said.
By late Friday, both the dollar and Treasuries had rebounded somewhat.
